newsitem.title: UK: Britain tries to stop Caribbean money-laundering.
newsitem.headline: Britain tries to stop Caribbean money-laundering.

text.p: Britain may take extra powers over its five dependent territories in the Caribbean to try to stop money-laundering by drugs barons, government sources said on Wednesday.

Foreign Office minister Sir Nicholas Bonsor said Britain had examined "actual or potential problems" in the territories -- Bermuda, the British Virgin Islands, the Cayman Islands, Montserrat and the Turks and Caicos Islands.
"Considerable improvements are being made in the administration of the territories and their good government," he said in answer to a parliamentary question.
"However, it has become clear that some extension of those powers which may be exercised by (Britain) may be needed."
The sources said Britain had encouraged the local governments in the territories to introduce legislation against money-laundering on the lines of those existing in Britain.
One source said the extra powers might act as a "form of stimulus" to governments to put such legislation in place.

Some of the British dependent territories have already pledged to bring in such laws. A Turks and Caicos Islands official said last month he expected legislation to be passed there by the end of the year.
